results.notes: PASS means locally judged coherent enough for literary research reading, not an independent-human pass or authenticity/admission finding. Read all prose of chapters 85-87, lines 1-264 (129 prose paragraphs), including the ending. The deterioration accumulates through meals, sleep, changing visit etiquette and paper rather than one bad message; "从宫中丧讯传到如今，已过了几个月。" (86, line 101) and the further months in 87 avoid a same-night death/wedding collapse. Daiyu keeps teasing, preferences and ordinary tomorrow-plans; "没什么。早上都是说明日的事。" (86, line 165) is an effective retrospective death-voice, not a final testament. The thin-cup plan, cool medicine and paper preservation carry loss materially. Reservations: the nursing ledger and repeated corrections of soup, fabric, pillows and staffing sometimes prolong one lesson instead of changing the emotional relation. Backup medical help is sought quite late in the final day, and Baoyu, found nearby with only two title slips left, arrives after several post-death tasks; the text permits this but would benefit from more felt elapsed travel time. Marriage is knowingly to Baochai, not a concealed substitution, but "我知道，是宝姐姐。既议定了，我依长辈的意思。" (87, line 203) reads as acquiescence to an already decided arrangement, not the clearest affirmative choice. "别说娶个人便能治病，人家女孩儿不是药。" (87, line 197) is ethically legible but conspicuously programmatic. The prose asserts permission for a restrained family rite while mourning continues; I did not verify historical law or medical facts. All concerns are reading notes, not automatic rejection. The packet supplies no separate sample objects, so sample_checks is empty rather than invented.

PASS is a local research-reading opinion only. Read the complete 85-87 sequence, lines 1-318 (156 prose paragraphs), in five nonoverlapping sequential blocks. "如此又过了两个月。" (86, line 113) explicitly lengthens the illness beyond chapter 85; further months and the distinction between expired initial restrictions and continuing mourning make chapter 87 legible without implying historical verification. Baoyu is away with his father at the ritual venue; the missed carriage route supplies a real communication obstacle, although the repeated pursuit is visibly serving the late-arrival plot. Two doctors see Daiyu before the death, and "医者重又察看，停了片刻，才轻轻摇头。" (86, line 171) keeps confirmation separate from servants guessing. Incomplete swallowing, the unaltered poem, repaired soft collar and residual habits make the death persuasive. However, "屋里没有谁说一段等着旁人记住的话。" (86, line 169) explains the intended anti-testament aesthetic instead of entirely trusting the scene. This token most clearly stages Baoyu being asked, taking time and then saying "我愿意照所议的办，只求不要急在眼下。" (87, line 237). Baochai has understood the situation and is not merely a restorative appliance; reciprocal physical closeness, furniture negotiations and the meal show an actual couple, without proving consummation. Several permission/expense/worker-duty explanations and explicit protections of names, papers and boundaries feel constraint-conscious. A strong research-readable sequence with pacing and narrative-explication reservations, not a complete human qualification, source claim, numerical score or overall winner. No packet-bound sample objects: sample_checks is empty.

PASS applies only to this model literary-research reading. Read every paragraph of chapters 85-87, lines 1-256 (125 prose paragraphs). The 85-to-86 dawn transition is direct, the illness already spans repeated ten-day intervals and seasonal clothing changes, and 87 explicitly waits further months; calendar resolution is looser than the tokens with a seven-month anchor or an extra stated two months. Daiyu sounds notably resistant to being reduced to care procedures: "正是要没用处的，有用处的你们背着我说够了。" (85, line 49). Her wit, clothing choices and unfinished ordinary poem give the quiet death individuality. Baoyu actually visits on the last morning and returns during the doctor visit; his later departure to arrange the doctor transport gives lateness a care-driven irony, but also makes the precisely timed absence feel more author-arranged than unavoidable. "一阵极细的呼吸过去，隔了很久，没有接来。" (86, line 145) earns restraint without a declamatory death speech. Medication identity is unusually auditable: "盖布还是煎新药时那一块，剩药仍有大半碗。" (86, line 151); this is internally clear but the adjacent dose, payment and container assurances can sound like custody documentation. Marriage notification is explicit: "我今儿叫你来，是先与你说清楚，不是等到那一天才说。" (87, line 185). Yet Baoyu mainly asks about rooms/books and never gives as clear an affirmative marital assent as in the strongest comparison; informed awareness is not the same thing as a fully dramatized choice. Family-rite permission is stated, not historically checked. The wedding-day walk, meal and final bedside proximity are coherent, with no forced cure for grief. These are substantive reservations, not fatal contradictions or automatic rejection; no human-admission/authenticity judgement and no fabricated sample checks.

PASS is limited to coherent literary research reading by this model. Read the full sequence through its final paragraph, lines 1-308 (151 prose paragraphs). The May rain and two subsequent monthly medicine lists connect well to "元春身后的丧务，自初时忙乱至今，已过了七个月。" (86, line 103); 87 adds further months and extends beyond the first married day. This is a clear internal calendar, not a verified historical mourning timetable. The ledger has human limits: "我这里只怕记漏，不是要一声声数。姑娘嫌烦呢。" (85, line 41). Daiyu retains minute interests almost to silence; "新粥明儿再吃，今儿先放一放。" (86, line 149) gives tomorrow its ordinary weight. The afternoon doctor and later recall avoid a single diagnostic miracle, though the messenger bounce through Baoyu's changing whereabouts visibly engineers his lateness. Marriage assent is conventional and explicit: "儿子知道，凭老太太和太太作主。" (87, line 231), less deliberative than a token that lets him request time. Continuing mourning and specifically permitted family rites are distinguished in the text. This token gives the new couple unusually useful differences: "你既爱这个，不必都说和我一样。" (87, line 295), unlike tastes in rice/tea, a book-bag repair disagreement and different quilt preferences. Baochai is less flattened into frictionless competence. Reservations: it still repeatedly explains who knew what, why supplies were adequate and which expense was legitimate; the late-arrival/cold-medicine/paper/wedding/needlework architecture is conspicuously shared by the four readings. Some construction remains visible, but no hard sequence-breaking contradiction compelled rejection. No original-authenticity or complete-human-pass claim; no separate samples in packet, so sample_checks is empty.
